before.title: Local Cauchy development of the adopted Einstein field law for smooth constrained data in the selected matter sectors
before.statement:
Adopt the direct-equation presentation of the classical gravitational framework
for a model satisfying the spacetime and classical-domain postulate
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the field-and-matter postulate
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], with the field law
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]: on the matter domain of the model,
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \kappa=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$
with $T$ the stress-energy tensor of the model's selected matter sector. Let the
sector be one of:

1. vacuum with cosmological constant ($T=0$);
2. the scalar-field model $(\varphi,V,K)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]
   with a chosen smooth potential whose scalar equation and stress tensor are
   those defined there;
3. the perfect-fluid model of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] with a
   smooth barotropic equation of state satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and
   $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on the range of the data;
4. the dust model of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with rest density $\rho\ge0$
   and prescribed smooth future unit velocity.

Let $(\Sigma,h,K)$ with the sector's smooth initial data (respectively nothing,
$(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$, $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$, $(\rho_0,U_0)$) satisfy the constraint
equations [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the sector's
stress tensor. Then the model admits a **local Cauchy development**: there are
a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of the framework and
a spacelike embedded image of $\Sigma$ inducing $(h,K)$ and the stated matter
data, solving the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ and the
sector's matter equations on a neighborhood of $\Sigma$; $\Sigma$ lies in the
interior of its domain of dependence; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to an isometry fixing the data and the time
orientation. The development is local in time and no uniform-in-the-data
existence time or global statement is asserted.
before.physical_scope: Classical general relativity in the smooth high-regularity branch: four-dimensional smooth Lorentzian geometry of signature (-+++), cosmological constant Lambda, and one of the classical matter sectors — vacuum, a scalar field with smooth potential, a barotropic perfect fluid with 0<p'<1, or geodesic dust — with smooth constrained initial data; the conclusion is a local-in-time development before any flow crossing, and makes no statement about nature, no global or all-time existence, no non-smooth, boundary, shock or asymptotic regime, and no claim of optimal Sobolev threshold.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.2 (Uniqueness): geometric uniqueness up to diffeomorphism, proved by putting two developments into the same harmonic-map gauge and invoking the uniqueness theorem for the reduced symmetric hyperbolic system

citations.quote:
Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework the
following statements.

**(i) Spacetime model.** The spacetime of a model of the framework is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: a smooth four-manifold $M$ without
boundary, a Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and a time orientation $N$. Its points represent
idealized physical events; the vector $N$ fixes which causal directions are
future-directed; and the causal classification of tangent vectors along any
worldline is the classification of the Lorentz vector spaces $(T_pM,g_p)$
together with the future/past convention of the time orientation. The metric
$g$ is the gravitational field of the model: it is the object that the field
law of the framework constrains, and its curvature is the model's
representation of gravity. The rules by which ideal clocks, test bodies and
light rays couple to $g$ are adopted separately as physical assumptions of the
framework.

**(ii) Classical domain.** Geometry and matter are treated as classical
continuum fields: the model describes macroscopic configurations of matter and
a classical metric, with no quantum description of either. The framework makes
no claim that a real spacetime is exactly such a manifold, that matter is
exactly a classical continuum, or that the smooth description applies to
arbitrarily small scales or arbitrarily strong fields; those are domain
limitations of the model family, not consequences of it.

**(iii) Unity of the model.** A model of the framework is specified by its
geometry $(M,g,N)$ together with its matter content and the field law adopted
for it; the geometry alone selects no matter configuration and no dynamics
(the matter assumptions are
adopted separately, in the companion postulate on matter content). Physical
parameters enter through
the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no
numerical value of a constant is asserted here.

**(iv) Smooth-branch restriction.** The fields of a model are defined on an
open domain of $M$; the metric is $C^\infty$ on all of $M$ and $M$ has no
boundary. Configurations in which a field fails to be smooth on a nonempty open
set, in which matter is concentrated on a lower-dimensional set in a way that
produces a distributional stress-energy tensor, or in which $M$ carries a
boundary, are outside the stated smooth domain of the framework and require
mathematics not supplied by these postulates.

**(v) Status.** These are adopted assumptions. They are not derived from the
mathematics of manifolds, from any symmetry principle, or from experiment; the
equivalence principle and covariance arguments motivate but do not prove them.
Testing the framework means comparing predictions computed from a fully
specified model — geometry, matter content and field law — with observations,
and agreement is evidence about the model, not a proof of these postulates.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], the following statements
about the matter content of a model.

**(i) Matter content is model input.** A model of the framework specifies its
nongravitational fields or matter and their explicit equations of motion and
couplings. The geometric data $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and covariance of the model's equations
under relabelling of events do not select those fields, equations or couplings:
different matter specifications over the same geometry are different models of
the framework, and no dynamical selection principle is asserted.

**(ii) Smooth matter and its stress-energy tensor.** The matter of a model on
its matter domain is represented by smooth fields on an open domain
$U\subseteq M$, and the model's stress-energy tensor is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ of
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], with the unit reading recorded there.
The relation of $T$ to the matter fields is part of the model: a model derived
from an action defines $T$ as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action,
while a model that prescribes $T$ directly is a separate source model.

**(iii) Consistency with the field law.** Where a model prescribes $T$
independently of matter fields, the prescription is admissible only if it meets
the consistency conditions imposed by the gravitational field law adopted for
the model, stated where that law is stated; in the action formulation the
matter equations, their coupling to the metric, and the on-shell conservation
of $T$ are derived within the model rather than assumed. Conservation is an
on-shell statement about a specified model and is not automatic for an
arbitrary smooth symmetric $T$.

**(iv) Energy conditions are optional additional assumptions.** A model may
adopt any of the pointwise inequalities of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] as
further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. None of them is a consequence
of the preceding clauses, of the field law, or of the symmetry of $T$; each
model records which conditions, if any, it adopts, and a model that adopts none
is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that it is divergence-free
exactly on the solutions of the scalar equation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither statement, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). No positivity of
$\varepsilon$ or of $p$ is required or implied. A model may carry the
additional data of an **equation of state**: a function
$P:D_P\to\mathbb R$ on a subset $D_P\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor and derived fields.** The model's
**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

a smooth symmetric contravariant $2$-tensor field ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). The **comoving
derivative**, **expansion** and **acceleration** of $n$ are

$$D f:=n^a\partial_af\quad(f\in C^\infty(U)),\qquad \vartheta:=\nabla_an^a,\qquad a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b ,$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

The physical reading of $\varepsilon$ and $p$ as a rest-frame energy density
and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

**(c) Fluid equations.** The **perfect-fluid equations** on $U$ are

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

That the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free if and only if these two
equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain**, carrying its
restricted smooth structure
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The physical reading of $\rho$ as a rest-mass density in a unit system, and of
$u$ as the four-velocity congruence of the matter, is fixed by the framework's
matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal
$n$, induced metric $h$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$G$ and $S$ be the Einstein tensor and scalar curvature of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then, at every $p\in\Sigma$
and for all tangential vectors $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z);$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g\bigl(R^g(X,Y)Z,n\bigr)=(\nabla^h_XK)(Y,Z)-(\nabla^h_YK)(X,Z);$$

**(c) normal projections.**
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12\bigl(S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2\bigr),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK);$$

**(d) constraint equations.** If in addition the field equation
$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$ for a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ and
constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
for every tangential $Y$.

Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential and initial data
   $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$;
3. **strict barotropic perfect fluid:** a model with smooth $p=p(\epsilon)$ and
   $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$, with initial data
   $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]);
4. **geodesic dust:** a model $(\rho,u)$ as in [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]
   with initial data $(\rho_0,U_0)$, $\rho_0\ge0$ and $U_0$ a smooth
   future-directed unit timelike field on $\Sigma$.

Then in each branch there is a smooth local development with the properties
established in the corresponding item, [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]
(branch 2), [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] (branch 3),
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] (branch 4) and, for branch 1, the vacuum
instance of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g$ with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$, solving
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ with the branch's stress tensor and matter
equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

derivations.claim: (Identification of the equations.) Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework the
following statements.

**(i) Spacetime model.** The spacetime of a model of the framework is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: a smooth four-manifold $M$ without
boundary, a Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and a time orientation $N$. Its points represent
idealized physical events; the vector $N$ fixes which causal directions are
future-directed; and the causal classification of tangent vectors along any
worldline is the classification of the Lorentz vector spaces $(T_pM,g_p)$
together with the future/past convention of the time orientation. The metric
$g$ is the gravitational field of the model: it is the object that the field
law of the framework constrains, and its curvature is the model's
representation of gravity. The rules by which ideal clocks, test bodies and
light rays couple to $g$ are adopted separately as physical assumptions of the
framework.

**(ii) Classical domain.** Geometry and matter are treated as classical
continuum fields: the model describes macroscopic configurations of matter and
a classical metric, with no quantum description of either. The framework makes
no claim that a real spacetime is exactly such a manifold, that matter is
exactly a classical continuum, or that the smooth description applies to
arbitrarily small scales or arbitrarily strong fields; those are domain
limitations of the model family, not consequences of it.

**(iii) Unity of the model.** A model of the framework is specified by its
geometry $(M,g,N)$ together with its matter content and the field law adopted
for it; the geometry alone selects no matter configuration and no dynamics
(the matter assumptions are
adopted separately, in the companion postulate on matter content). Physical
parameters enter through
the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no
numerical value of a constant is asserted here.

**(iv) Smooth-branch restriction.** The fields of a model are defined on an
open domain of $M$; the metric is $C^\infty$ on all of $M$ and $M$ has no
boundary. Configurations in which a field fails to be smooth on a nonempty open
set, in which matter is concentrated on a lower-dimensional set in a way that
produces a distributional stress-energy tensor, or in which $M$ carries a
boundary, are outside the stated smooth domain of the framework and require
mathematics not supplied by these postulates.

**(v) Status.** These are adopted assumptions. They are not derived from the
mathematics of manifolds, from any symmetry principle, or from experiment; the
equivalence principle and covariance arguments motivate but do not prove them.
Testing the framework means comparing predictions computed from a fully
specified model — geometry, matter content and field law — with observations,
and agreement is evidence about the model, not a proof of these postulates.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], the following statements
about the matter content of a model.

**(i) Matter content is model input.** A model of the framework specifies its
nongravitational fields or matter and their explicit equations of motion and
couplings. The geometric data $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and covariance of the model's equations
under relabelling of events do not select those fields, equations or couplings:
different matter specifications over the same geometry are different models of
the framework, and no dynamical selection principle is asserted.

**(ii) Smooth matter and its stress-energy tensor.** The matter of a model on
its matter domain is represented by smooth fields on an open domain
$U\subseteq M$, and the model's stress-energy tensor is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ of
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], with the unit reading recorded there.
The relation of $T$ to the matter fields is part of the model: a model derived
from an action defines $T$ as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action,
while a model that prescribes $T$ directly is a separate source model.

**(iii) Consistency with the field law.** Where a model prescribes $T$
independently of matter fields, the prescription is admissible only if it meets
the consistency conditions imposed by the gravitational field law adopted for
the model, stated where that law is stated; in the action formulation the
matter equations, their coupling to the metric, and the on-shell conservation
of $T$ are derived within the model rather than assumed. Conservation is an
on-shell statement about a specified model and is not automatic for an
arbitrary smooth symmetric $T$.

**(iv) Energy conditions are optional additional assumptions.** A model may
adopt any of the pointwise inequalities of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] as
further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. None of them is a consequence
of the preceding clauses, of the field law, or of the symmetry of $T$; each
model records which conditions, if any, it adopts, and a model that adopts none
is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that it is divergence-free
exactly on the solutions of the scalar equation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither statement, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). No positivity of
$\varepsilon$ or of $p$ is required or implied. A model may carry the
additional data of an **equation of state**: a function
$P:D_P\to\mathbb R$ on a subset $D_P\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor and derived fields.** The model's
**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

a smooth symmetric contravariant $2$-tensor field ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). The **comoving
derivative**, **expansion** and **acceleration** of $n$ are

$$D f:=n^a\partial_af\quad(f\in C^\infty(U)),\qquad \vartheta:=\nabla_an^a,\qquad a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b ,$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

The physical reading of $\varepsilon$ and $p$ as a rest-frame energy density
and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

**(c) Fluid equations.** The **perfect-fluid equations** on $U$ are

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

That the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free if and only if these two
equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain**, carrying its
restricted smooth structure
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The physical reading of $\rho$ as a rest-mass density in a unit system, and of
$u$ as the four-velocity congruence of the matter, is fixed by the framework's
matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal
$n$, induced metric $h$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$G$ and $S$ be the Einstein tensor and scalar curvature of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then, at every $p\in\Sigma$
and for all tangential vectors $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z);$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g\bigl(R^g(X,Y)Z,n\bigr)=(\nabla^h_XK)(Y,Z)-(\nabla^h_YK)(X,Z);$$

**(c) normal projections.**
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12\bigl(S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2\bigr),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK);$$

**(d) constraint equations.** If in addition the field equation
$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$ for a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ and
constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
for every tangential $Y$.

Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential and initial data
   $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$;
3. **strict barotropic perfect fluid:** a model with smooth $p=p(\epsilon)$ and
   $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$, with initial data
   $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]);
4. **geodesic dust:** a model $(\rho,u)$ as in [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]
   with initial data $(\rho_0,U_0)$, $\rho_0\ge0$ and $U_0$ a smooth
   future-directed unit timelike field on $\Sigma$.

Then in each branch there is a smooth local development with the properties
established in the corresponding item, [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]
(branch 2), [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] (branch 3),
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] (branch 4) and, for branch 1, the vacuum
instance of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g$ with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$, solving
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ with the branch's stress tensor and matter
equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.
